::: {.why}
The price gap you found last night is the practical content of the whole week: calibration to today's vanillas does not pin down the dynamics, and every exotic price is a bet on which dynamics are right.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Name something local volatility and stochastic volatility disagree about, and the observable that would tell them apart.
- Report the price of one exotic under both models and express the gap as a fraction of its price.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Quantify the disagreement across a family: price forward-starting options and barrier options at several parameters under both calibrations, and report the gaps. Forward-starting options are the sharpest case because they depend directly on the future smile, which is exactly what the two models disagree about.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Name the observable: the two models imply different dynamics for the at-the-money volatility as a function of the spot, which is measurable from a time series of surfaces. Run that measurement on whatever surface history you have and say which model it favours, with the caveat that a few weeks of data will not settle it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the conclusion for the milestone: calibration quality on vanillas says nothing about which model to use for anything else, which is the most useful sentence in this week.
:::
:::
